The bear argues that True Green Bio Energy Ltd's Price-to-Book (P/B) ratio of 3.96x is significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 3.31x [E7], suggesting an overvaluation. However, this comparison does not fully capture the company’s performance and potential. For instance, the company has a Return on Equity (ROE) of 22.8% for the last year, which is notably higher than the sector benchmark of 12.23% [E9] and even the median return over the past three years at 8% [E27]. This recent strong performance indicates that investors might be justified in paying a premium. Additionally, while the bear points out that the company’s ROE has been lower than the sector average over the last three years [E60], it is important to note that the most recent year shows a 23% return on equity [E28]. This suggests an improvement and potential for sustained profitability. Therefore, the elevated P/B ratio might be justified by the company’s strong recent performance. Moreover, the stock trades at a Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio of 20.1x, which is higher than the sector benchmark of -19.89x [E6]. This indicates that investors are willing to pay more for earnings, possibly due to the company’s growth prospects and profitability. The fact that the stock sits 93% of the way up its 52-week range also suggests strong investor interest in the company [E5]. In conclusion, while historical performance is important, recent and current metrics suggest that True Green Bio Energy Ltd might be under-appreciated given its strong ROE and P/E ratio relative to sector benchmarks.

The bull argues that True Green Bio Energy Ltd's recent strong ROE of 22.8% [E28] justifies its P/B ratio of 3.96x [E7]. However, this argument is weakened by the company’s historical performance. The median return on equity over the past three years was only 4% [E26], and even more recently, it has been as low as 3% [E13] over ten years. This suggests that the recent high ROE might be an anomaly rather than a sustainable trend. Furthermore, while the P/E ratio of 20.1x is higher than the sector benchmark of -19.89x [E6], this comparison is not entirely relevant given that the sector benchmark itself appears negative. The bull’s point about investor interest indicated by the stock trading near its 52-week high [E5] does not necessarily mean the valuation is justified, especially when considering other metrics like ROE.
